text:
Riley Chen: heads-up — saw steady mem growth on the longctx perf run (10k tokens) when int8 kv is enabled. baseline (bf16) stayed at ~6.2G, int8 path climbed to ~11.1G over the session. 

Priya Kapoor: whoa, that's pretty big. same model and batch config?

Riley Chen: same model, batch=1, kernel selection enabled. only change was quant profile = int8-symmetric + kv-compression.

Tom Alvarez: can you paste the perf hotspots from the run? especially page faults / mmap churn.

Riley Chen: sure, cpaste from perf-top + dmesg during repro: 

```
- major page faults spike when slot eviction runs (~every 3s)
- kernel: runtime/kernel_selector.cpp:choose_gemm_path() falls back from fused-gemm to slice-gemm at ~1.2M seq processed
- slab allocator: repeated slab->mmap->munmap for freed pages (fragmentation pattern)
```

Alex Morgan: fragmenting slab + int8 pages might cause allocator to request new mmaps instead of reusing slots. int8 pages are smaller but more numerous so coalescing matters.

Priya Kapoor: did the telemetry show slot residency distribution? cold vs hot vs dormant?

Riley Chen: yes — residency histogram: many tiny slots (256B-1KB) pinned as "dormant" due to quantized key alignment. eviction loop checks by timestamp but quantized slots weren't coalesced, so eviction scanned more metadata and ended up doing more mmaps.

Tom Alvarez: that scan cost could explain kernel selector fallback. increased latency -> runtime switches to safer kernel to keep latency SLOs -> that kernel has higher working-set and touches more memory -> more page faults. feedback loop.

Riley Chen: exactly. reproduced with a minimal repro: long prompt with many short turns producing KV churn. repro script: 

```
python tools/repro_longctx.py --model xlarge --quant int8 --turns 1200 --prompt-size 8
```

Priya Kapoor: what's the accuracy delta when we enable int8 kv? any quality regressions?

Riley Chen: micro-evals show ~0.7% drop on the reranking set when int8+no-warmup. With warmup (prefetch first 128 tokens into kv) drop goes to ~0.2%.

Alex Morgan: useful signal — suggests warmup/prefetch mitigates precision-induced drift. Also coalescing/migration of small slots into contiguous pages would reduce mmap churn.

Tom Alvarez: two-pronged mitigation proposal: 
- increase coalescing window for quantized slots (merge nearby small slots every N seconds)
- change eviction policy to prefer consolidating small dormant slots before unmapping pages

Riley Chen: I ran a quick patch (coalesce_window=5s) — memory growth now capped at ~7.4G for the same repro. page-fault spikes still happen but less frequently. perf trace shows a ~40% reduction in slab mmap calls.

Priya Kapoor: perf numbers?

Riley Chen: latency p50/p95 unchanged more than noise. token throughput dropped ~3% (batching heuristics slightly different), but cost saving on mmap syscalls and less kernel fallback frequency.

Alex Morgan: suggest another tweak: when kernel selector sees repeated fallbacks, mark the model instance as "high-frag" and switch to an alternate kernel that is fragmentation-friendly (lower memory working set) to avoid oscillation. Also add metric: kv_page_unmaps_per_minute.

infra-bot: deploy request submitted by Riley Chen for branch kv/coalesce-int8-quickfix to staging · build #4821 · status: queued

Tom Alvarez: we should also run the longctx soak with mixed quant (bf16 keys, int8 values) — might buy precision where we need it and reduce key alignment fragmentation.

Riley Chen: noted. next steps checklist: 
- [ ] run mixed quant soak (24h) on staging (Tom)
- [ ] bake coalescing patch in canary + add kv_page_unmaps_per_minute metric (Priya)
- [ ] experiment with prefetch window heuristics; default warmup tokens=128 (Alex)
- [ ] add kernel-selector circuit-breaker to avoid fallback loops (Riley)

Priya Kapoor: will open a short PR with metrics + config flags. keeping defaults conservative.

Alex Morgan: thanks — good catch. this pattern (small-slot explosion under int8) feels like a new class of fragmentation bug for long-lived sessions. :eyes:

Riley Chen: logging repro and perf dumps to /prod-artifacts/kv-int8-longctx-1865010200.tar.gz and linking in the PR.

Tom Alvarez: lgtm. if staging soak is clean we can push to dedicated clusters.

Riley Chen: updating the repro to include forced kernel warm path to verify warmup helps accuracy. will report numbers tomorrow.
